B08C001.summary: After Drona falls, the Kaurava leaders spend a sleepless night grieving and regretting their treatment of the Pandavas. Karna is made commander, fights for two days, and is finally killed by Arjuna, and Sanjaya carries the news back to Dhritarashtra. Janamejaya then asks how the old king could go on living after hearing of so many deaths.

scenes.B08C001S01: The Kaurava camp after Drona's death, Karna's appointment and death in battle, and Janamejaya's question about Dhritarashtra's grief.

shots.B08C001S01H01: Opening invocation to Narayana, Nara and Sarasvati, with the word Jaya.
shots.B08C001S01H02: Duryodhana and the other Kaurava leaders grieve through the night, make Karna commander, fight two days, and see Karna killed by Arjuna. Sanjaya then reports to Dhritarashtra.
shots.B08C001S01H03: Janamejaya asks how Dhritarashtra could keep living after hearing of Karna's death and the earlier losses, and asks to hear the full account.

B08C002.summary: Sanjaya returns to the palace and finds Dhritarashtra stricken with grief. He reminds the king of the good advice he rejected and asks whether he feels any pain. Sanjaya then urges calm, saying that fate cannot be resisted, and Dhritarashtra accepts this and asks for the full account of the battle.

scenes.B08C002S01: Sanjaya's return to Dhritarashtra, his rebuke of the king, the appeal to fate, and the king's request for the whole story.

shots.B08C002S01H01: Sanjaya reaches the palace, bows to the grieving king, and asks whether Dhritarashtra regrets rejecting the counsel of Vidura, Krishna and others.
shots.B08C002S01H02: Dhritarashtra mourns Bhishma, Drona and Karna, asks what his own side did when the army broke, and asks how the Pandavas fought.
shots.B08C002S01H03: Sanjaya tells him not to grieve, since a wise man does not suffer over what fate brings and human plans may or may not succeed.
shots.B08C002S01H04: Dhritarashtra says he accepts that all this is fate and asks Sanjaya to tell him everything.

B08C003.summary: Sanjaya describes the Kaurava army stunned and disheartened after Drona's death. Duryodhana rallies them with a speech that mocks Arjuna and praises Karna. He names Karna commander, and Karna fights fiercely until Arjuna kills him.

scenes.B08C003S01: The stunned Kaurava army, Duryodhana's speech urging them on, and Karna's brief command and death.

shots.B08C003S01H01: Sanjaya describes Drona's sons and the rest of the army as pale, silent and dejected, with weapons falling from their hands. Duryodhana then speaks to rouse them, praising Karna and boasting that Arjuna is a coward.
shots.B08C003S01H02: Duryodhana makes Karna commander. Karna fights hard, slaughters many enemies, and is at last killed by Arjuna.

B08C004.summary: On hearing the news Dhritarashtra faints, and the royal women lament loudly until Sanjaya and Vidura revive him. Once he recovers he asks whether Duryodhana has died. Sanjaya answers that Karna and Duhshasana have been killed, and that Bhimasena drank Duhshasana's blood in anger.

scenes.B08C004S01: Dhritarashtra's collapse and revival, his question about Duryodhana, and Sanjaya's report of Karna's and Duhshasana's deaths.

shots.B08C004S01H01: Dhritarashtra falls senseless at the news, the women wail, and Sanjaya and Vidura revive the king and comfort the household. The king then sits silent, censures his sons and praises the Pandavas, and questions Sanjaya.
shots.B08C004S01H02: Dhritarashtra asks whether Duryodhana has already gone to Yama's abode, and asks Sanjaya to tell him the truth.
shots.B08C004S01H03: Sanjaya replies that Karna and his kinsmen have been slain, that Duhshasana was killed by a son of Pandu, and that Bhimasena drank his blood in anger.

B08C005.summary: Dhritarashtra asks Sanjaya to name who among the Kurus and Pandavas are still alive. Sanjaya lists a long roll of the fallen on both sides, from Bhishma and Drona to countless named princes and nameless soldiers. He ends by comparing Arjuna's killing of Karna to gods slaying demons, and by blaming the disaster on Dhritarashtra's own policy and sons.

scenes.B08C005S01: Dhritarashtra's request for a list of the living and dead, Sanjaya's long roll of the fallen, and his closing blame of the king.

shots.B08C005S01H01: Dhritarashtra, troubled by grief, asks Sanjaya to name who among the Kurus and Pandavas are still alive and who have died.
shots.B08C005S01H02: Sanjaya lists the fallen heroes one by one, including Bhishma, Drona, Karna, Duryodhana's brothers and allies, Bhagadatta, Jayadratha, and many kings and their troops. He compares Arjuna's killing of Karna to Indra slaying Vritra, and closes by blaming the disaster on Dhritarashtra's own evil policy and his sons.

B08C006.summary: Dhritarashtra asks for the names of the Pandava warriors who have been killed by his side. Sanjaya gives a long roll of the Pandava and allied dead, most of them slain by Bhishma or Drona, and including Abhimanyu and his allies. The list is offered as a grim tally of the costs of the battle.

scenes.B08C006S01: Dhritarashtra asks for the names of the Pandava dead, and Sanjaya reads out a long list of those killed by the Kaurava side.

shots.B08C006S01H01: Dhritarashtra asks Sanjaya to name the Pandava warriors killed by his own side, having already heard the list of his own dead.
shots.B08C006S01H02: Sanjaya lists the Pandava and allied dead, naming the killers in each case: Abhimanyu's death at the hands of many warriors, the kings Virata and Drupada killed by Drona, and many others. He ends by saying he has told all that was asked.

B08C007.summary: Dhritarashtra despairs that his army will be wiped out and asks who is still alive on his side. Sanjaya lists the Kaurava warriors who remain on the field, including Ashvatthama, Kritavarma, Shalya and Duryodhana himself. Dhritarashtra reads from this that the Kauravas will lose, and he collapses in grief.

scenes.B08C007S01: Dhritarashtra's despair, Sanjaya's roll of surviving Kaurava warriors, the king's conclusion about the outcome, and his collapse.

shots.B08C007S01H01: Dhritarashtra says he sees no hope for the rest of his army after the deaths of Bhishma, Drona and Karna, and asks who among his side is still alive.
shots.B08C007S01H02: Sanjaya lists the Kaurava warriors still on the field, including Ashvatthama, Kritavarma, Shalya, Gautama, the king of the Gandharas, the sons of Dhritarashtra and Karna, and Duryodhana himself, all ready to fight.
shots.B08C007S01H03: Dhritarashtra says that from these facts he can see plainly which side will win.
shots.B08C007S01H04: Vaishampayana says the king swoons when he learns how few of his army remain. He comes to, asks Sanjaya to wait, and then collapses to the ground.

B08C008.summary: Janamejaya asks what Dhritarashtra said after hearing of Karna's death. Vaishampayana describes the king's stunned lament, which runs through Karna's great strength, his past victories for Duryodhana, and his skill as a warrior. Dhritarashtra ends by saying he has no will to go on living after such a loss.

scenes.B08C008S01: Janamejaya's question, and Dhritarashtra's long lament for Karna and his own grief.

shots.B08C008S01H01: Janamejaya asks what the king said after hearing of Karna's fall and the loss of his sons, and asks to hear all of it.
shots.B08C008S01H02: Vaishampayana describes the king's stunned lament, in which he praises Karna's strength and his conquests for Duryodhana, mourns his death at Arjuna's hands, and says he has no wish to live.

B08C009.summary: Sanjaya urges Dhritarashtra to bear his grief, but the king gives way to a long lament. He blames destiny, mourns Karna and Duhshasana, and recalls how Duryodhana rejected Bhishma's and Yudhishthira's advice to make peace. He then asks a stream of questions about how Karna fell and who stood by him, and his despair is the emotional centre of the section.

scenes.B08C009S01: Sanjaya's words of comfort and Dhritarashtra's long lament, which ends in a flood of questions about Karna's death and the battle.

shots.B08C009S01H01: Sanjaya praises Dhritarashtra as wise and learned, and urges him to summon his courage and not give way to grief.
shots.B08C009S01H02: Dhritarashtra replies at great length. He blames destiny, calls Karna's death incredible, and wonders why he himself has not died of grief. He mourns Karna and Duhshasana, recalls Bhishma's and Yudhishthira's advice that Duryodhana ignored, and compares his own state to a bird with clipped wings. He then asks how Karna was killed, who stood by him, and how each of the Kaurava leaders reacted, ending by asking for a full account of the final fight.

B08C010.summary: After Drona's fall the Kaurava army is rallied, and the leaders hold a council at evening. Ashvatthama urges that Karna be made commander, and Duryodhana persuades Karna to take the post, which Karna accepts with confidence. Karna is installed with ritual and blessings and leads the army out at sunrise.

scenes.B08C010S01: The evening council after Drona's fall, Ashvatthama's advice, Karna's acceptance of command, and his installation and departure at sunrise.

shots.B08C010S01H01: Sanjaya describes the day's end: after Drona's death and the defeat of Ashvatthama's plans, Duryodhana rallies the retreating troops until dusk, then the Kauravas gather in their camp to take counsel.
shots.B08C010S01H02: Duryodhana asks his leaders for their opinions on what must be done.
shots.B08C010S01H03: Ashvatthama says the Kauravas should not despair and proposes Karna as commander. Duryodhana, pleased, appeals to Karna to take up the post, citing Karna's past service and the fall of Bhishma and Drona.
shots.B08C010S01H04: Karna accepts, saying he will vanquish the Pandavas and that Duryodhana should consider them already defeated.
shots.B08C010S01H05: The formal installation of Karna follows, with ritual vessels, blessings from Brahmanas, and praises. Karna sets out the army at sunrise, and Sanjaya compares him to a second sun.

B08C011.summary: Karna takes the field at dawn and draws up the Kaurava army in a crocodile-shaped formation, with named commanders at each part of the body. Yudhishthira urges Arjuna to kill Karna, and Arjuna answers with a half-moon formation of his own. Both sides believe the other is as good as beaten, and the armies rush together to begin the fight.

scenes.B08C011S01: Dhritarashtra's question, Karna's appearance and the makara formation, and Yudhishthira's order of battle for the Pandavas.

shots.B08C011S01H01: Dhritarashtra asks Sanjaya what Karna did after taking command and receiving the king's encouragement.
shots.B08C011S01H02: Sanjaya describes the noise of the Kaurava army preparing before dawn, Karna's splendid car and conch, and the crocodile-shaped formation, with Karna at its beak and named leaders at its eyes, head, neck, body, feet and tail.
shots.B08C011S01H03: Yudhishthira tells Arjuna that Karna is the only real threat left on the Kaurava side and urges him to kill Karna. Arjuna forms a half-moon array, both sides think the other already defeated, and the armies rush together.

B08C012.summary: The two armies clash in a chaotic slaughter of men, elephants, horses and chariots. Bhima, riding an elephant, fights the Kulutas king Kshemadhurti, also on an elephant, and after a long exchange kills him. Seeing their leader fall, the Kaurava troops flee.

scenes.B08C012S01: The general carnage, the Pandava advance, and the duel between Bhima and Kshemadhurti that ends with Kshemadhurti's death and the Kaurava rout.

shots.B08C012S01H01: Sanjaya describes the bloody general fighting, the Pandava forces advancing with their allies, and Bhima on his elephant. The duel between Bhima and Kshemadhurti on elephants goes back and forth until Bhima kills Kshemadhurti's elephant and then Kshemadhurti himself, and the Kaurava troops flee.

B08C013.summary: Karna and the Pandava leaders fight across the field in many separate duels. Satyaki takes on the Kaikeya brothers Vinda and Anuvinda, kills Anuvinda, and after a sword fight slays the other Kaikeya prince. The Kaikeya army then breaks and scatters.

scenes.B08C013S01: The pairings of the leading warriors, Satyaki's fight with the Kaikeya brothers, and the rout of the Kaikeya army.

shots.B08C013S01H01: Karna cuts down Pandava ranks while the Pandavas attack the Kauravas. The leaders pair off in duels, among them Nakula against Karna, Bhima against Drona's son and Satyaki against the Kaikeya brothers. Satyaki kills Anuvinda, then fights Vinda and the other Kaikeya prince on foot with swords and kills the prince, and the Kaikeya army flees.

B08C014.summary: Srutakarman kills Citrasena in single combat, and Prativindhya defeats and kills Citra, first turning aside Citra's weapons. The Kaurava troops, now leaderless, scatter in all directions. Only Drona's son charges forward alone against Bhima.

scenes.B08C014S01: The duels of Srutakarman and Citrasena and of Prativindhya and Citra, the rout of the Kaurava troops, and Drona's son's solo charge at Bhima.

shots.B08C014S01H01: Srutakarman and Citrasena duel until Srutakarman cuts off Citrasena's head, and his troops flee. Prativindhya fights Citra, deflects Citra's dart and mace, and kills him with a lance. The Kaurava troops scatter, and Drona's son alone rushes at Bhima.

B08C015.summary: Bhima and Ashvatthama fight a long, evenly matched duel, each matching the other's arrows and weapons. Heavenly beings marvel at both, comparing them to destroying forces at the end of an age. Both are finally struck down, and their drivers carry each one from the field.

scenes.B08C015S01: The duel between Ashvatthama and Bhima, the heavenly praise for both, and the removal of the two wounded warriors by their drivers.

shots.B08C015S01H01: Sanjaya describes the evenly matched duel between Ashvatthama and Bhima, with each side countering the other's weapons and arrows, heavenly beings marvelling, and both warriors finally falling senseless to be carried off by their drivers.

B08C016.summary: Dhritarashtra asks for an account of Arjuna's fight against the Samsaptakas and against Ashvatthama. Sanjaya describes Arjuna's slaughter of the Samsaptaka army, the heavenly voice that identifies Krishna and Arjuna as Nara and Narayana, and Ashvatthama's challenge to Arjuna to fight him as a guest. Arjuna turns from his enemies to meet Ashvatthama.

scenes.B08C016S01: Dhritarashtra's request, Arjuna's slaughter of the Samsaptakas, and Ashvatthama's challenge that draws Arjuna away to fight him.

shots.B08C016S01H01: Dhritarashtra asks Sanjaya to describe Arjuna's battle with the Samsaptakas and with Ashvatthama, and the battles of the other kings against the Pandavas.
shots.B08C016S01H02: Sanjaya describes Arjuna cutting down the Samsaptaka army, with chariots, elephants and men falling. Gods and heavenly beings praise him and Krishna, a voice names them as Nara and Narayana, and Ashvatthama calls Arjuna out to fight as a guest. Arjuna asks Krishna which duty to take up first, and Krishna drives him to Ashvatthama. Ashvatthama wounds both, and Arjuna cuts through all his arrows, then turns from the Samsaptakas to face Ashvatthama.

B08C017.summary: Arjuna and Ashvatthama fight a fierce duel, with Arjuna at first holding back out of respect for his teacher's son. Krishna urges him to kill Ashvatthama, and Arjuna then wounds him badly and cuts the traces of his horses. Ashvatthama is carried from the field, and Arjuna and Krishna turn back to the Samsaptakas.

scenes.B08C017S01: The duel between Arjuna and Ashvatthama, Krishna's urging, Ashvatthama's withdrawal, and Arjuna's return to the Samsaptakas.

shots.B08C017S01H01: Sanjaya describes the duel between Arjuna and Ashvatthama, the wounds on both sides, and the slaughter of many Samsaptakas and other troops by Arjuna. Krishna tells Arjuna to stop sparing Ashvatthama. Arjuna then badly wounds him and cuts his horses' traces, so the horses carry Ashvatthama away. Ashvatthama retreats to Karna's army, and Arjuna and Krishna return to the Samsaptakas.

B08C018.summary: Krishna drives Arjuna to the northern part of the field, where the Magadha chief Dandadhara is massacring Pandava troops from the back of a huge elephant. Arjuna cuts down the king, his brother Danda and their elephants, and the enemy army breaks. His followers praise him, and he goes back to fight the Samsaptakas.

scenes.B08C018S01: Arjuna's duel with the Magadha chief Dandadhara and his brother Danda, and the rout of the enemy elephants and troops.

shots.B08C018S01H01: Sanjaya describes Krishna turning the chariot to the north to face Dandadhara, who rides an elephant and is slaughtering troops. Arjuna cuts off Dandadhara's arms and head, kills his elephant, then kills Danda and his elephant. The enemy elephants are destroyed, the army breaks, and Arjuna's allies praise him before he returns to the Samsaptakas.

B08C019.summary: Arjuna continues to cut down the Samsaptakas and the Kaurava allies, and he rides over the carnage like a man crossing a sea on a bridge of his own weapons. Krishna then points out the battlefield to him, listing the scattered weapons, armour, jewels and dead bodies. On their return they hear the Kaurava side in uproar and see the king of Pandya destroying the army.

scenes.B08C019S01: Arjuna's continued slaughter, Krishna's tour of the battlefield, and the sight of Pandya's assault on the army.

shots.B08C019S01H01: Sanjaya describes Arjuna cutting down many warriors, cars, elephants and horses, while the samsaptakas and Kaurava allies press in on him. Krishna urges Arjuna to finish off the Samsaptakas and go after Karna. Krishna then shows Arjuna the battlefield, cataloguing the weapons, armour, ornaments and corpses. Returning to camp, they hear uproar from the Kaurava side and see Pandya attacking the army, cutting down many foes.

B08C020.summary: Dhritarashtra asks about the Pandya king, whose feats he has not heard. Sanjaya explains that Pandya rated himself above the great warriors and wrecked Karna's army. Ashvatthama challenges him, and after a long duel Ashvatthama kills Pandya, his elephant and his followers.

scenes.B08C020S01: Dhritarashtra's request, Sanjaya's account of Pandya's assault, his duel with Ashvatthama, and Pandya's death.

shots.B08C020S01H01: Dhritarashtra asks Sanjaya to describe in full the feats, spirit and pride of the Pandya hero he has mentioned before.
shots.B08C020S01H02: Sanjaya says Pandya thought himself greater than the foremost warriors, and describes him routing Karna's army and killing many allies. Ashvatthama challenges him, and their duel goes on with arrows, weapons and chariots, until Ashvatthama kills Pandya's elephant, cuts off his arms and head, and kills his followers. The Kaurava kings then honour Ashvatthama.

B08C021.summary: With Pandya dead, Dhritarashtra asks what Arjuna did next. Krishna warns Arjuna that Yudhishthira has withdrawn and that Karna is slaughtering the Srinjayas, so Arjuna urges the charioteer on. The battle becomes a general melee, and Karna mows down Pancala and Pandava fighters in a huge bloody slaughter.

scenes.B08C021S01: Dhritarashtra's question, Krishna's warning about Yudhishthira and Karna, and the general melee in which Karna kills many Pancala and Pandava warriors.

shots.B08C021S01H01: Dhritarashtra asks what Arjuna did after Pandya fell and Karna was routing the foe, saying Arjuna is his greatest fear.
shots.B08C021S01H02: Sanjaya reports that Krishna tells Arjuna the king and the other Pandavas have withdrawn, and that Karna is slaughtering the Srinjayas. Arjuna has Krishna drive on, and a fierce general battle breaks out. Karna kills many Pancala warriors and their chariots, and the bodies of men, horses and elephants pile up across the field.

B08C022.summary: Kaurava elephant-fighters attack Dhrishtadyumna, and the Pandava allies rush to save him. Satyaki and the younger Pandava brothers kill many of the elephants and their riders. Sahadeva kills the Pundra elephant, and Nakula kills the Anga chief, who is driving an elephant, and the Kaurava elephant force is broken.

scenes.B08C022S01: The elephant attack on Dhrishtadyumna, the Pandava counter-attack, and the killing of the Anga and Pundra leaders and their elephants.

shots.B08C022S01H01: Sanjaya describes the Kaurava elephant-warriors from many kingdoms attacking Dhrishtadyumna. Pandava allies rush to rescue him, and Satyaki kills the elephant of the Vanga king and then its rider.
shots.B08C022S01H02: Sahadeva kills the elephant of the Pundra king with three arrows, then advances on the Anga chief.
shots.B08C022S01H03: Nakula stops Sahadeva and kills the Anga chief and his elephant. The Anga and allied elephant-men attack, and a long fight follows in which Sahadeva and Nakula kill more elephants. The Kaurava force flees, and the Pandava leaders turn on Karna.

B08C023.summary: Sahadeva and Duhshasana, brothers on opposite sides, fight a long duel with arrows and swords. Sahadeva wounds Duhshasana, who falls senseless, and his driver carries him off. Sahadeva then turns on Duryodhana's division and begins to crush it.

scenes.B08C023S01: The duel between Sahadeva and Duhshasana, Duhshasana's retreat, and Sahadeva's attack on Duryodhana's division.

shots.B08C023S01H01: Sanjaya describes the duel: the brothers trade arrows, each cutting down the other's weapons, a sword is thrown and deflected, and at last Sahadeva's shaft pierces Duhshasana, who swoons and is driven from the field. Sahadeva then begins to destroy Duryodhana's division, as a man in anger crushes ants.

B08C024.summary: Nakula meets Karna in a long duel. Nakula taunts Karna as the root of the war, and Karna answers that a true hero should fight without boasting. Karna wins the exchange, disarms and humiliates Nakula, and then lets him go out of regard for Kunti's words. Karna goes on to rout the Pancala chariots, and the battlefield is strewn with wreckage and dead.

scenes.B08C024S01: The duel between Nakula and Karna, Karna's mercy to Nakula, and Karna's rout of the Pancala army.

shots.B08C024S01H01: Long account of the duel and its aftermath. Nakula taunts Karna, and Karna answers with a rebuke about boasting. Their fight with bows and arrows fills the sky until Karna cuts Nakula's chariot and horses to pieces and leaves him on foot with a club. Karna disarms him, humiliates him, then lets him go, recalling Kunti's words. Nakula returns in shame to Yudhishthira, and Karna goes on to scatter the Pancalas, leaving the field strewn with broken chariots, elephants, horses and corpses, while the Pandava troops flee.

B08C025.summary: Uluka and Yuyutsu fight a hard duel, and Uluka wins by cutting down Yuyutsu's standard, driver and horses. Satanika and Srutakarman destroy each other's chariots in a close exchange. Shakuni and Sutasoma fight on foot after Sutasoma's chariot is wrecked, and Shakuni breaks Sutasoma's scimitar and bow, then rampages through the Pandava ranks.

scenes.B08C025S01: The duels of Uluka and Yuyutsu, Srutakarman and Satanika, and Shakuni and Sutasoma, and Shakuni's rout of the Pandava troops.

shots.B08C025S01H01: Sanjaya describes Uluka defeating Yuyutsu in a long duel, then Srutakarman and Satanika fighting until both lose their chariots. Shakuni fights Sutasoma, who battles on foot with a sword until Shakuni breaks it. Shakuni then routs the Pandava divisions, as Indra scattered the Daitya army.

B08C026.summary: Kripa holds off Dhrishtadyumna, who is so shaken that his charioteer turns him away toward Arjuna and Bhima. Kritavarma fights Shikhandi, wounds him badly and sends him from the field. The Pandava army then flees.

scenes.B08C026S01: Kripa's fight with Dhrishtadyumna, and Kritavarma's duel with Shikhandi that drives the Pandava army from the field.

shots.B08C026S01H01: Kripa checks Dhrishtadyumna and wounds him repeatedly until he is dazed. His charioteer turns the car away, and Kripa pursues him, blowing his conch. Warriors on both sides remark on Kripa's power.
shots.B08C026S01H02: Shikhandi fights Kritavarma. Both are wounded, and Kritavarma's arrow strikes Shikhandi down. Shikhandi's driver carries him off, and the Pandava army breaks and flees.

B08C027.summary: Arjuna routs a large force made up of the Trigartas, Samsaptakas and others, including several kings. Satyasena wounds Krishna with a lance, and Arjuna kills Satyasena in return and goes on to slay many others. He finally uses a heavenly weapon that brings down a huge number of troops, and the field is strewn with bodies.

scenes.B08C027S01: Arjuna's attack on the Trigartas and Samsaptakas, Satyasena's wound to Krishna, and Arjuna's use of the Aindra weapon.

shots.B08C027S01H01: Sanjaya describes Arjuna scattering the Trigartas, Samsaptakas and their allies, and killing several kings in turn. Satyasena wounds Krishna's arm, and Arjuna beheads Satyasena and kills others. When the Samsaptakas surround him, Arjuna uses the Aindra weapon, and the field is covered with wreckage and corpses. The enemy force is almost wiped out, and Arjuna shines like a fire without smoke.

B08C028.summary: Yudhishthira and Duryodhana fight a fierce duel, and Yudhishthira wrecks Duryodhana's horses, chariot and weapons. Karna, Drona's son and Kripa rush to save Duryodhana, and a general melee breaks out. The fighting turns into a frenzy of killing, in which friends and enemies alike are slaughtered, and the day ends in great carnage.

scenes.B08C028S01: The duel of Yudhishthira and Duryodhana, the rescue attempt, and the general melee that ends the afternoon's fighting.

shots.B08C028S01H01: Yudhishthira fights Duryodhana, wounds him, destroys his chariot and weapons, and leaves him on foot in danger. Karna, Drona's son and Kripa hurry to his aid, and the Pandava brothers gather to fight them. The battle becomes a frenzy of elephants, horses and men, with many killed in every grim manner, and Karna, Arjuna and Bhima slaughter the Pancalas, Trigartas and Kuru elephant divisions respectively, as the sun passes its height.

B08C029.summary: Dhritarashtra, sure the Kauravas are finished, asks Sanjaya to describe the afternoon fight between Yudhishthira and Duryodhana. The two kings duel fiercely, trading shafts and a dart, until Yudhishthira's dart knocks Duryodhana senseless. Bhima, bound by his vow, stops Yudhishthira from finishing him, and Bhima then turns on Kritavarma, who has come to Duryodhana's aid.

scenes.B08C029S01: Dhritarashtra's request, the duel of Yudhishthira and Duryodhana, and Bhima's intervention to spare Duryodhana.

shots.B08C029S01H01: Dhritarashtra says the Kauravas are as good as dead, and asks how Yudhishthira and Duryodhana fought in the afternoon battle.
shots.B08C029S01H02: Sanjaya describes the duel: Duryodhana cuts Yudhishthira's bow, the two trade arrows and a dart and a mace is raised, and Yudhishthira's dart fells Duryodhana. Bhima reminds Yudhishthira of his vow and stops him from finishing Duryodhana. Kritavarma comes up to help, and Bhima attacks him with a golden mace.

B08C030.summary: Karna leads the Kaurava army back into a fierce fight with the Pandavas, and the field is littered with dead men and animals. Arjuna and Krishna return, and Arjuna scatters the Kaurava forces, cutting down Duryodhana's and others' weapons. Karna keeps fighting until the sun sets, and both armies withdraw into darkness and dust. Carrion creatures gather over the battlefield.

scenes.B08C030S01: Karna's counterattack, Arjuna's return and destruction of the Kaurava forces, and the close of the day.

shots.B08C030S01H01: Sanjaya describes the bloody battle the Kauravas fight under Karna, the Pandava rout against Satyaki and Karna, Arjuna and Krishna charging in and scattering the Kaurava army, and Karna fighting on until his forces are nearly wiped out.
shots.B08C030S01H02: Sanjaya describes the sunset, the Kauravas withdrawing with their army in fear of a night battle, the Pandavas returning in triumph, and the Rakshasas and beasts gathering over the battlefield.

B08C031.summary: Dhritarashtra hears that Arjuna has beaten his army and asks what the Kauravas did next. Sanjaya tells how the defeated Kauravas take counsel, and Karna proposes to meet Arjuna next morning with his own bow Vijaya and Shalya as his charioteer. He lists his strengths and Arjuna's, and Duryodhana agrees to the plan. Dhritarashtra laments his sons' fate, and Sanjaya rebukes him for the wrongs that began the war.

scenes.B08C031S01: Dhritarashtra's question and grief, Sanjaya's rebuke, and Karna's long speech asking Duryodhana for Shalya as charioteer.
scenes.B08C031S02: Duryodhana's agreement to Karna's plan and his approach to Shalya.

shots.B08C031S01H01: Dhritarashtra says Arjuna has defeated every warrior single-handed, praises the Kauravas for fighting such a man, and asks what Duryodhana did next.
shots.B08C031S01H02: Sanjaya describes the battered Kauravas returning to camp to take counsel. Karna, angry, says Arjuna was alert and had been helped by Krishna, and promises to defeat him next day. Duryodhana agrees, and the army rests and marshals a fresh array.
shots.B08C031S01H03: Dhritarashtra asks how Karna will fight next and laments that his trust in Karna and Shakuni has come to nothing, and that fate is supreme.
shots.B08C031S01H04: Sanjaya rebukes the king for the dice match and the other wrongs he allowed, and tells him not to dwell on the past. He says the king was warned and ignored counsel, so the slaughter has come, and he begins the account of the night's events.
shots.B08C031S01H05: Karna tells Duryodhana he will fight Arjuna next morning, and claims he has weapons equal to Arjuna's, as well as the bow Vijaya, which Rama gave him. He admits that Arjuna has the better charioteer in Krishna and the better bow Gandiva, and asks that Shalya be made his driver, with spare arrows and an escort of chariots. He says he will then be superior to Arjuna.
shots.B08C031S02H01: Duryodhana agrees with Karna's wishes and promises chariots, arrows and an escort, saying the kings will follow Karna into battle.
shots.B08C031S02H02: Duryodhana turns to address Shalya, the king of the Madras, as the scene closes.

B08C032.summary: Duryodhana humbly asks Shalya, king of the Madras, to become Karna's charioteer, flattering him and pointing to the losses of Bhishma and Drona. Shalya is insulted and furiously refuses, saying he will not serve a son of a charioteer. Duryodhana soothes him with praise and an appeal to his truthfulness, and Shalya finally agrees, on condition that he may speak freely during the fight.

scenes.B08C032S01: Duryodhana's request to Shalya, Shalya's angry refusal, Duryodhana's flattery, and Shalya's conditional agreement.
scenes.B08C032S02: Karna and Duryodhana accept Shalya's terms.

shots.B08C032S01H01: Duryodhana humbly asks Shalya to drive Karna's chariot against Arjuna. He argues that Bhishma and Drona have fallen, that Karna is the army's remaining hope, and that Shalya should guard Karna as Krishna guards Arjuna.
shots.B08C032S01H02: Shalya, outraged, stands up in anger, with knitted brows and rolling eyes.
shots.B08C032S01H03: Shalya says Duryodhana insults him by asking him to drive. He refuses, saying he does not rank Karna as his equal, speaks of the castes and the proper duties of a Kshatriya, and asks leave to go home.
shots.B08C032S01H04: Duryodhana holds him back and flatters him, saying he never lies, that he is known as a barbed arrow to his foes, and that he is as good as Krishna.
shots.B08C032S01H05: Shalya is pleased and agrees to drive Karna's chariot in the battle with Arjuna, on condition he may say what he likes to Karna during the fight.
shots.B08C032S02H01: Duryodhana and Karna accept Shalya's terms and agree.

B08C033.summary: Duryodhana begins a long tale that he says the sage Markandeya told his father, about a war between the gods and the Asuras. Three Asura brothers win a boon from the creator god and have three flying cities built, which a magic lake can revive when their dead are thrown into it. Indra fails to break the cities, and the gods go to the creator and then to Shiva, who is praised with many names and asked for help.

scenes.B08C033S01: Duryodhana's myth of the three Asura cities and the gods' appeal to Shiva, and a publisher's header line that closes the section.

shots.B08C033S01H01: Duryodhana tells Shalya a story from the sage Markandeya about a battle between the gods and the Asuras. The three sons of Taraka win boons, Maya builds three cities for them, and Hari's lake revives slain Asuras. Indra cannot break the cities, so the gods seek help from the creator, who says only one arrow from a god can destroy them. The gods take refuge with Shiva, praise him with many names, and ask him what he will do for them.
shots.B08C033S01H02: Publisher's header line for the Gutenberg edition, not part of the narrative.

B08C034.summary: Duryodhana continues his tale for Shalya. The gods ask Shiva to destroy the Danavas, and after a round of bargaining over how much energy each side will give, Shiva is armed with a cosmic chariot built from the parts of the universe. Brahma drives it, and Shiva burns the three cities and their Asura inhabitants. Duryodhana then tells how Rama, son of Jamadagni, gained his weapons from Shiva and passed them to Karna, and he argues that Karna must be of noble birth, not the son of a charioteer.

scenes.B08C034S01: Brahma's praise of Shiva and the opening exchange in which the gods and Shiva each offer to fight with only part of their might.
scenes.B08C034S02: The gods' pooling of energy, the building of Shiva's chariot, the drive against the three cities, Duryodhana's appeal to Shalya, and the story of Rama's weapons.
scenes.B08C034S03: Duryodhana's claim that Rama taught Karna the use of weapons and that Karna is of noble birth.

shots.B08C034S01H01: Duryodhana says that after the fears of the gods and sages were calmed, Brahma praised Shiva and asked him to destroy the Danavas.
shots.B08C034S01H02: Shiva replies that he will not fight alone, and that the gods should combine their forces with half his might.
shots.B08C034S01H03: The gods answer that the Danavas are twice as strong as they are.
shots.B08C034S01H04: Shiva says he will use half his energy against the enemies if the gods will do the same.
shots.B08C034S01H05: The gods reply that they cannot bear half of Shiva's energy, and ask him to use half of their combined strength instead.
shots.B08C034S02H01: Shiva agrees to fight with half of the gods' combined energy.
shots.B08C034S02H02: The gods accept, Shiva becomes greater than all beings, and is named Mahadeva. He asks for a chariot and bow for the battle.
shots.B08C034S02H03: The gods build a huge chariot from the parts of the universe, with the earth as its body, the mountains as axle and wheels, and the Vedas and sacred things as its guardians, bow and arrow and steeds all assembled.
shots.B08C034S02H04: Brahma agrees to drive the chariot. Shiva rides out, and when the chariot sinks Vishnu lifts it as a bull. Shiva shoots his arrow, the three cities burn and fall into the western ocean, and the gods go home. Duryodhana then urges Shalya to drive Karna as Brahma drove Rudra, and starts another story about Rama.
shots.B08C034S02H05: Duryodhana tells how Rama, son of Jamadagni, pleased Shiva with long penances and was given weapons. Rama later killed many Danavas for the gods and was given more weapons by Shiva in return.
shots.B08C034S03H01: Duryodhana says Rama taught all his weapons to Karna, and argues that Karna is probably a son of a god born into the Kshatriya order and abandoned as an infant, and could not have been born into the Suta caste.

B08C035.summary: Duryodhana urges Shalya to drive Karna's chariot as Brahma drove Rudra, and Shalya recalls the story and agrees, while warning that Krishna will step in if Arjuna falls. Duryodhana praises Karna and belittles Arjuna, and Shalya accepts on condition that he may speak his mind freely to Karna. Shalya then boasts that he can drive as skilfully as Matali, Indra's charioteer.

scenes.B08C035S01: Duryodhana's appeal by the story of Brahma and Rudra, Shalya's warnings, Duryodhana's praise of Karna, and Shalya's conditional acceptance.
scenes.B08C035S02: Shalya's acceptance and self-praise, and Karna's brief reply.

shots.B08C035S01H01: Duryodhana says Brahma drove Rudra in the same way, and asks Shalya to hold the reins of Karna's horses in the same spirit.
shots.B08C035S01H02: Shalya recalls hearing the old story of Brahma and Rudra, notes that Krishna knows such things, and warns that Krishna will fight himself if Arjuna falls.
shots.B08C035S01H03: Duryodhana praises Karna as the best of warriors, lists his feats against the Pandavas, and urges Shalya to fight for him as Krishna serves the Pandavas.
shots.B08C035S01H04: Shalya agrees to drive for Karna, provided he may say what he likes to Karna during the battle.
shots.B08C035S01H05: Karna and Duryodhana accept, and Duryodhana embraces Karna. Karna asks Duryodhana to plead with Shalya once more, which Duryodhana does with a loud, persuasive appeal.
shots.B08C035S02H01: Shalya embraces Duryodhana, promises to do what he can, and asks Karna to forgive any blunt words he may say.
shots.B08C035S02H02: Karna tells Shalya to serve their cause as Brahma serves Ishana and Keshava serves Partha.
shots.B08C035S02H03: Karna's words continue with the same comparison to Keshava serving Partha.
shots.B08C035S02H04: Shalya says that self-praise is usually improper, but he will say that he is as skilled as Matali and can handle Karna's horses in battle, so Karna need not worry.

B08C036.summary: At dawn Shalya mounts Karna's chariot, and Karna mounts beside him, the two shining together like sun and fire. Duryodhana urges Karna to seize Yudhishthira or kill the other Pandavas, and Shalya rebukes Karna for speaking so lightly of Arjuna. Karna brushes aside the warning and orders the chariot forward.

scenes.B08C036S01: Duryodhana's praise of Shalya, the dawn departure, Duryodhana's exhortation, and Shalya's rebuke of Karna.

shots.B08C036S01H01: Duryodhana tells Karna that Shalya, who is greater than Krishna, will drive the chariot as Matali drives Indra's, and that they can surely beat the Parthas.
shots.B08C036S01H02: At morning Duryodhana again asks Shalya to guide Karna's horses. Shalya agrees, the chariot is prepared and blessed, and Karna and Shalya mount. Duryodhana then urges Karna to seize Yudhishthira or kill Arjuna and the Pandava brothers, and Karna boasts that Shalya's driving will help him defeat Partha.
shots.B08C036S01H03: Shalya answers Karna's boast by reminding him how formidable the Pandavas are, with Arjuna's Gandiva and Yudhishthira and the twins raining arrows like clouds, and warns Karna that he will not talk so proudly when he hears them.
shots.B08C036S01H04: Sanjaya says that Karna, ignoring Shalya's warning, speaks to him.
shots.B08C036S01H05: Karna begins a reply to Shalya, and the speech continues into the next scene.

B08C037.summary: As Karna sets out, omens of disaster appear, but the Kauravas cheer and call the Pandavas as good as defeated. Karna boasts that he alone can face Arjuna, recalls Drona's death, and declares he will fight regardless of fate. Shalya laughs at him and praises Arjuna's old feats, and Karna retorts that Shalya's praise will be proved right only if Arjuna beats him. Karna then drives toward the Pandava army, searching for Arjuna.

scenes.B08C037S01: The omens, Karna's boast and the words of Shalya and Karna.
scenes.B08C037S02: Karna's advance toward the Pandava army in search of Arjuna.

shots.B08C037S01H01: Sanjaya lists the omens as Karna sets out: earthquakes, meteors, storms, birds and beasts passing to the right, the horses falling, bones raining down, and weapons and banners trembling. The Kauravas, blind to the omens, cheer Karna, and Karna, recalling Bhishma and Drona, declares he will face Arjuna alone, regardless of his fate, and describes the chariot and weapons Rama gave him.
shots.B08C037S01H02: Sanjaya says that Shalya, mocking Karna's boasting, laughs aloud at him.
shots.B08C037S01H03: Shalya tells Karna to stop his bragging, and recalls Arjuna's old feats: his fights with Bhava, the rescue of Duryodhana, the defeat of the Gandharvas, and his victory over Karna in the cattle raid on Virata's kine.
shots.B08C037S01H04: Sanjaya says that Karna, angered by Shalya's praise of his enemy, answers him.
shots.B08C037S01H05: Karna says Shalya may praise Arjuna, but the praise is only deserved if Arjuna defeats him in the coming battle.
shots.B08C037S02H01: Shalya gives no answer. Karna tells him to proceed, and the chariot sets off against the enemy, and Karna looks for Arjuna among the Pandava army.

B08C038.summary: As Karna goes out to battle, he offers Pandava soldiers escalating rewards for showing him Arjuna, from jewels and cattle up to villages, women and horses, and finally promises to kill Krishna and Arjuna and give away their wealth. The Kaurava army cheers, and Shalya laughs in scorn at Karna's boasting.

scenes.B08C038S01: Karna's offer of rewards to any Pandava who will point out Arjuna, the cheering Kaurava army, and Shalya's mockery.

shots.B08C038S01H01: Karna tells every Pandava soldier he meets that whoever shows him Arjuna will be rewarded with wealth, cattle, villages, cars, elephants, horses, women and more. If that is not enough, he will kill Krishna and Arjuna and give their wealth to the finder. Karna blows his conch, the Kauravas rejoice, and Shalya laughs at his boasting.

B08C039.summary: Shalya tells Karna that giving away his wealth is folly and that he is courting death by challenging Arjuna. Karna replies that he will seek Arjuna with his own strength and will not be turned back by anyone. Shalya answers with a long string of comparisons, calling Karna a jackal, a frog and a hare facing a lion, a tiger or an elephant.

scenes.B08C039S01: Shalya's warning about Karna's gifts and challenge, Karna's refusal to give way, and Shalya's long comparisons mocking Karna's courage.

shots.B08C039S01H01: Shalya tells Karna not to give away a golden chariot and its bulls, says the gift is foolish, and urges him to fight Arjuna with his army instead of boasting, since his time seems to be running out.
shots.B08C039S01H02: Karna replies that he seeks Arjuna relying on his own arms, and that Shalya, a foe in friend's clothing, cannot make him turn back, not even Indra with his thunder could do that.
shots.B08C039S01H03: Shalya mocks Karna's challenge at length, comparing him to a jackal, hare, frog, calf, dog and snake that foolishly takes on a lion, tiger, elephant or bird, and says Karna will be shown to be the lesser when Arjuna's bow sounds in battle.

B08C040.summary: Karna, stung by Shalya's taunts, answers with fury. He boasts of a special shaft he is saving for Arjuna or Krishna and claims he can defeat both. He then launches a long, abusive attack on the Madrakas, Shalya's people, and threatens to crush Shalya's head with his mace if he speaks again. He ends by ordering Shalya to drive on.

scenes.B08C040S01: Karna's angry reply, his boast of a special shaft, his abusive attack on the Madrakas, and his order to proceed.

shots.B08C040S01H01: Sanjaya says Karna, rebuked by Shalya, grows furious and answers him.
shots.B08C040S01H02: Karna says Shalya has no merit to judge Arjuna or Krishna, then boasts of a special shaft he has kept for Arjuna or Krishna alone, which he expects will kill them both. He calls Shalya a fool born in a sinful country, insults the Madrakas at length and their women and customs, says he is ready to die in battle, and threatens to crush Shalya's head with his mace if he speaks again. He ends by ordering Shalya to drive on.

B08C041.summary: Shalya tells Karna a fable of a crow fed on the leftovers of a merchant's children, who grows so proud that it challenges a swan to a flying contest. The crow tires over the open ocean and is saved by the swan, and the crow learns humility. Shalya applies the lesson to Karna, who has grown proud on the Kauravas' favours, and urges him to seek the protection of Krishna and Arjuna.

scenes.B08C041S01: Shalya's fable of the crow and the swan, and his application of it to Karna's pride and past defeats.

shots.B08C041S01H01: Shalya introduces a fable about a crow fed on scraps by a merchant's children on the far side of the ocean. The crow becomes proud, and when swans arrive it challenges their leader to a flight contest, which the swans mock.
shots.B08C041S01H02: The swan and the crow take to the sky. The crow shows off many motions, while the swan flies in one steady manner. The crow seems to be winning, but then the swan flies far over the ocean, the crow tires and finds no island to rest on, and he begs for rescue.
shots.B08C041S01H03: The swan takes the exhausted crow on his back and carries him back to land, and the crow gives up his pride. Shalya applies it to Karna, pointing out Karna's past defeats at Virata's city and elsewhere, and urges him to seek the protection of Krishna and Arjuna, since they are far superior.

B08C042.summary: Karna dismisses Shalya's warnings and says he will fight Arjuna and Krishna regardless. He recalls how, having posed as a Brahmana to learn weapons from Rama, he was cursed to forget his great weapon when most in need, and he vows to use the brahmastra against Arjuna. He also recounts how he once killed a Brahmana's calf and was cursed that his chariot wheel would sink in battle. He finally tells Shalya to be silent and listen.

scenes.B08C042S01: Karna's reply to Shalya, his recollection of Rama's curse and the calf curse, and his vow to fight Arjuna with the brahmastra.

shots.B08C042S01H01: Karna, unmoved, answers Shalya at length. He says he will face Krishna and Arjuna anyway, recalls being cursed by Rama for hiding his caste, and vows to kill Arjuna with the brahmastra he will be able to use. He then recalls killing a Brahmana's calf by accident and being told that his wheel would sink in battle, rejects Shalya's rebukes, and ends by telling him to be silent and hear what he has to say.

B08C043.summary: Karna says Shalya's words cannot frighten him, not even if all the gods joined Arjuna and Krishna. He says he was born for valour and glory, and that Shalya is spared only out of friendship, affection and the duty owed to an ally, and because of the agreement to overlook his insults. He declares that he could defeat his foes without a thousand Shalyas.

scenes.B08C043S01: Karna's reply to Shalya, in which he refuses to be frightened and explains why Shalya's life is spared.

shots.B08C043S01H01: Karna tells Shalya that words cannot scare him, that he was born to show valour and win glory, and that he spares Shalya for friendship, affection, alliance and the agreement he made. He says the task of serving Dhritarashtra depends on him, and that he would beat his foes without a thousand Shalyas.

B08C044.summary: Shalya dismisses Karna's boast as raving and says he alone can beat the enemy. Karna answers with even sharper words, quoting at length from Brahmanas who condemned the Vahikas, the Arattas and the Madrakas for their customs, drink, women and origins. The passage is a long, sneering catalogue of supposed regional faults.

scenes.B08C044S01: Shalya's brief dismissal, and Karna's long quotation of Brahmanas' tales that denounce the Vahikas, Arattas and Madrakas.

shots.B08C044S01H01: Shalya tells Karna that his boasts are raving and that Shalya could defeat the enemy without a thousand Karnas.
shots.B08C044S01H02: Sanjaya says Karna answers Shalya with words even more bitter than before.
shots.B08C044S01H03: Karna quotes a Brahmana's account, heard at Dhritarashtra's court, of the Vahikas: their supposed customs, their drinking, their women's singing and dancing, and the lands they live in. He follows this with more quoted Brahmanas, who say the Arattas, Madrakas and others have no virtue, and then gives a list of peoples he considers impure and ends with a bitter verdict on the Madrakas.

B08C045.summary: Karna goes on with more quoted tales, claiming that the Vahikas and Arattas are lawless and that Shalya, as their king, shares their faults. Shalya replies that every land has both good and bad people, and that Karna should cool his anger. Duryodhana then stops the quarrel, and Karna is calmed and tells Shalya to drive on.

scenes.B08C045S01: Karna's further quotations on the Vahikas, Madrakas and other peoples, Shalya's reply, and Duryodhana's intervention that ends the quarrel.

shots.B08C045S01H01: Karna quotes more Brahmanas and legends about lawless peoples and their customs, the Vahikas and Arattas, and Kalmashapada's curse against the Madrakas, and calls Shalya their king, who shares in their sins. He ends by telling Shalya to keep quiet, and says he will kill Krishna and Arjuna after killing Shalya.
shots.B08C045S01H02: Shalya replies that every land has both good and bad people, that Karna's own Angas have faults, and that he should drop his anger.
shots.B08C045S01H03: Sanjaya says Duryodhana stops the argument, begging Shalya and calming Karna, and Karna, smiling, tells Shalya to proceed.

B08C046.summary: Karna sets his own army against the Pandava array, drawn up by Dhrishtadyumna, and strikes at Yudhishthira. Dhritarashtra asks how the two armies were arranged and where each warrior stood. Sanjaya describes the Kaurava formation, the Pandava commanders assigned to their opponents, and Shalya's warnings as Arjuna's chariot advances, ending with the armies colliding.

scenes.B08C046S01: Karna's formation and attack on Yudhishthira, Dhritarashtra's question, the list of the two armies' positions, Yudhishthira's assignments, and Shalya's warning about Arjuna's approach.
scenes.B08C046S02: Shalya's reply to Karna's boast and the mingling of the two armies.

shots.B08C046S01H01: Sanjaya says that when Karna sees the Pandava array made by Dhrishtadyumna, he roars, makes his chariot rattle, and sets his troops in counter-array. He slaughters the Pandavas and strikes Yudhishthira with many arrows.
shots.B08C046S01H02: Dhritarashtra asks how Karna arrayed his forces against the Pandavas, who stood where, how the sons of Pandu arrayed theirs, and how Arjuna could be beaten in battle.
shots.B08C046S01H03: Sanjaya lists the Kaurava array: Kripa, the Magadhas and Kritavarma on the right, Shakuni and Uluka with Gandhara horsemen, the Samsaptakas on the left, the Kambojas, Sakas and Yavanas beyond them, Karna at the centre, then Duhshasana, Duryodhana with his brothers, Ashvatthama and the elephants. Yudhishthira then tells Arjuna to take measures against the array, and Arjuna promises to kill its foremost warriors.
shots.B08C046S01H04: Yudhishthira assigns his brothers and allies their targets: Arjuna against Karna, Bhima against Duryodhana, Nakula against Vrishasena, Sahadeva against Shakuni, Satanika against Duhshasana, Satyaki against Kritavarma, Pandya against Ashvatthama, and Yudhishthira himself against Kripa.
shots.B08C046S01H05: Sanjaya describes Arjuna's chariot advancing with Krishna as driver. Shalya points out the omens, the dust, the banners and the weapons, and tells Karna that Arjuna will soon be there. Karna answers that Arjuna is surrounded by the Samsaptakas and will be lost among them.
shots.B08C046S02H01: Shalya scoffs at Karna's boast of killing Arjuna and names the Pandava heroes Karna will face, including Bhima, Yudhishthira, the twins, Draupadi's sons, Dhrishtadyumna and Satyaki. The two armies then clash like the Ganga and Yamuna meeting.

B08C047.summary: Dhritarashtra asks Sanjaya to give a full account of the battle between Arjuna and the Samsaptakas and between Karna and the Pandavas. Sanjaya describes the Pandava array under Dhrishtadyumna and the Samsaptakas charging Arjuna, who cuts them down in great numbers. Kripa, Kritavarma, Shakuni and others fight the Pancalas and their allies, Duryodhana protects Karna, and Karna wounds Yudhishthira and slaughters many enemies.

scenes.B08C047S01: Dhritarashtra's request, the Samsaptaka attack on Arjuna, the wider battle, and Karna's slaughter of the Pandava forces.

shots.B08C047S01H01: Dhritarashtra asks how Arjuna attacked the Samsaptakas and how Karna fought the Pandavas, and asks for every detail, since he never tires of hearing of heroic deeds.
shots.B08C047S01H02: Sanjaya describes the Pandava army under Dhrishtadyumna and Draupadi's sons. The Samsaptakas charge Arjuna, who cuts down their ranks, and the battle is compared to his old fight with the Nivatakavachas. Kripa, Kritavarma and Shakuni fight the Pancalas and their allies, while Duryodhana protects Karna. Karna wounds Yudhishthira and kills thousands of foes, and the battle is like the old war of gods and Asuras.

B08C048.summary: Dhritarashtra asks how Karna broke into the Pandava ranks to reach Yudhishthira. Sanjaya describes Karna cutting down the Prabhadrakas, Pancalas and Cedis, and the Pandava princes rushing at him in a body. Karna's sons Sushena and Vrishasena fight to protect him, and Bhima kills one of his sons. Karna nonetheless fights his way through toward Yudhishthira's division.

scenes.B08C048S01: Dhritarashtra's question, and Sanjaya's account of Karna's slaughter, the duels of Karna's sons with the Pandavas, and Karna's advance toward Yudhishthira.

shots.B08C048S01H01: Dhritarashtra asks Sanjaya how Karna broke into the Pandava ranks and struck Yudhishthira, and who were the heroes Karna had to overcome before he could reach the king.
shots.B08C048S01H02: Sanjaya describes Karna's attack on the Pancalas and the din of the armies. Karna kills many Prabhadrakas, Cedis and Pancalas, while the Pandava heroes, led by Dhrishtadyumna, Satyaki and the sons of Draupadi, close in on him. Karna's sons Sushena and Vrishasena fight fiercely around their father. Bhima kills Bhanusena, another son of Karna, and then fights Sushena. Vrishasena is disarmed by Satyaki, and Duhshasana rescues him. Karna then drives into Yudhishthira's division, destroying thirty chariots of the Cedis, and wounds the king with arrows while the armies fight on.

B08C049.summary: Karna drives through the Pandava host toward Yudhishthira, but Pandava warriors hold him back and Yudhishthira taunts him as a charioteer's son. Yudhishthira pierces him with a deadly arrow and knocks him unconscious, but Karna recovers and kills Yudhishthira's wheel-guards, wounds the king, and destroys his bow and armour. Yudhishthira flees, and Karna is about to seize him when Shalya warns him off, so Karna lets him go with a mocking speech. The fighting then becomes a huge carnage in which the field runs with blood, and the Kaurava army eventually breaks.

scenes.B08C049S01: Karna's advance through the Pandava host, his duel with Yudhishthira, Yudhishthira's flight, Shalya's warning, and the bloody general fighting that follows.

shots.B08C049S01H01: Long account in which Karna cuts through the Pandava host, Yudhishthira mocks him and shoots him down, Karna recovers and kills Yudhishthira's wheel-guards, then wounds and disarms the king, who flees. Karna pursues, reaches out to seize him, and is stopped by Shalya, who warns that Yudhishthira's power would burn them both. Karna mocks Yudhishthira and lets him go. Yudhishthira then rallies his men, and the battle becomes a vast, bloody carnage, with a river of blood flowing across the field, until the Kaurava army is driven back in flight.

B08C050.summary: As the Kaurava army flees, Karna orders Shalya to drive at Bhima, who vows to kill Karna and asks Satyaki and Dhrishtadyumna to guard Yudhishthira. Karna mocks Bhima, says he really wants to face Arjuna, and agrees to fight Bhima first. Bhima and Karna duel fiercely until Bhima's great shaft wounds Karna, who collapses on his chariot, and Shalya drives him away while Bhima routs the Kaurava troops.

scenes.B08C050S01: The flight of the Kaurava army, Bhima's challenge to Karna, the taunts between Karna and Shalya, and Karna's defeat by Bhima.

shots.B08C050S01H01: Duryodhana tries to rally his fleeing army, and some Kaurava troops turn on Bhima. Karna orders Shalya to drive toward Bhima's chariot. Bhima asks Satyaki and Dhrishtadyumna to guard Yudhishthira, and vows to kill Karna or die in the attempt.
shots.B08C050S01H02: Shalya warns Karna that Bhima is blazing with fury, like the fire at the end of an age, and could overwhelm the three worlds.
shots.B08C050S01H03: Karna laughs at Bhima, recalling how Bhima killed Kichaka in Virata's city, and says he has long wished to face Arjuna, but will fight Bhima first. Shalya urges him on, and Karna agrees to drive at Bhima.
shots.B08C050S01H04: Bhima and Karna duel. Karna cuts Bhima's bow and wounds him, Bhima answers with a huge shaft that knocks Karna senseless on his chariot, and Shalya carries him off as Bhima routs the Kaurava troops.

B08C051.summary: Dhritarashtra asks what Duryodhana did after Karna was knocked down by Bhima. Duryodhana sends many brothers to shield Karna, and Bhima kills several of them, including Vivitsu, Vikata and Kratha. Karna returns to duel with Bhima, who loses his chariot and kills many elephants and horsemen on foot. Karna then pursues Yudhishthira, Satyaki comes to Bhima's aid, and the two armies collide in a vast melee at midday.

scenes.B08C051S01: Dhritarashtra's question, Duryodhana's brothers' defence of Karna, the renewed duel of Karna and Bhima, and the general melee that follows.

shots.B08C051S01H01: Dhritarashtra says that Bhima's defeat of Karna is an astonishing feat, reminds Sanjaya that Duryodhana always said Karna alone would destroy the Pandavas, and asks what Duryodhana did next.
shots.B08C051S01H02: Sanjaya describes Duryodhana sending his brothers to protect Karna. Bhima kills many of them, including Vivitsu, Vikata, Saha and Kratha, and then Nanda and Upananda, and the survivors flee. Karna drives back to face Bhima, and their duel is fierce. Karna cuts Bhima's bow and standard, and Bhima hurls a mace that Karna destroys. Bhima's chariot and driver are destroyed, and he fights on foot, crushing hundreds of elephants, cars and horsemen. Karna pursues Yudhishthira, Satyaki aids Bhima, and the two armies crash together in a huge, confused fight at midday.
shots.B08C051S01H03: Sanjaya says the battle becomes so loud and mutual with insults that he believes the warriors' time is running out, and that the Pandavas and Kauravas are now mangling each other with sharp shafts.

B08C052.summary: Sanjaya describes the general slaughter in grim detail. Every kind of troop meets every other, and the field is covered with blood, severed heads, limbs and dead animals, and it becomes a dust-filled chaos where friends cannot be told from foes. Rivers of blood flow past the corpses, carrion birds and beasts gather, and the Kaurava army weakens like a sinking ship.

scenes.B08C052S01: The general carnage of men and animals, the bloody rivers, the carrion creatures, and the collapse of the Kaurava army.

shots.B08C052S01H01: Sanjaya describes the chaotic slaughter of cars, horses, elephants and foot soldiers, the field covered with blood, heads and limbs, the dust that hides friend from foe, and the blood rivers thick with corpses. Carrion creatures gather in glee, heroes shout out their names and lineage, and the Kaurava army weakens like a sinking ship.

B08C053.summary: Arjuna turns to the Samsaptakas, Kosalas and Narayana forces, who are led by Susharma. Susharma wounds Krishna and Arjuna and cuts Arjuna's standard, but Arjuna paralyses the enemy with the Naga weapon, and Susharma frees them with the Sauparna weapon. After Susharma wounds Arjuna, Arjuna uses the Aindra weapon and slaughters thousands of warriors.

scenes.B08C053S01: Arjuna's fight against Susharma and the Samsaptakas, the Naga and Sauparna weapons, and the slaughter that follows the Aindra weapon.

shots.B08C053S01H01: Sanjaya describes Arjuna plunging into the Samsaptaka host and fighting Susharma, who wounds Krishna and cuts Arjuna's standard. The enemy then surrounds Arjuna's chariot, seizing Krishna and Arjuna, but Krishna throws them off. Arjuna blows his conch, Krishna answers, and Arjuna paralyses the Samsaptakas with the Naga weapon. Susharma calls up the Sauparna weapon, birds devour the snakes, and the enemy is freed. Susharma pierces Arjuna, who uses the Aindra weapon to slaughter thousands of warriors, and the Samsaptakas are finally outmatched.

B08C054.summary: The Kaurava leaders rush to rescue their broken army. Kripa fights Shikhandi, forcing him from his chariot, and then kills Suketu, son of Citraketu, when Suketu rushes to Shikhandi's aid. Dhrishtadyumna attacks Kritavarma, wounds him and kills his charioteer, and a fresh round of fighting breaks out.

scenes.B08C054S01: The Kaurava leaders rally, Kripa's duel with Shikhandi and the killing of Suketu, and Dhrishtadyumna's duel with Kritavarma.

shots.B08C054S01H01: Sanjaya says Kritavarma, Kripa, Drona's son, Karna, Uluka, Shakuni and Duryodhana try to rescue the army from Arjuna's onslaught, while Kripa's arrows cover the Srinjayas. Kripa fights Shikhandi, wounds him and kills his charioteer and horses, and Shikhandi attacks on foot with a sword before Suketu intervenes. Kripa kills Suketu, and Shikhandi withdraws. Meanwhile Dhrishtadyumna goes for Kripa, Kritavarma blocks him, Drona's son opposes Yudhishthira, and Duryodhana holds Nakula and Sahadeva while Karna confronts Bhima.
shots.B08C054S01H02: Kritavarma challenges Dhrishtadyumna, and the duel is as fierce as two hawks fighting over meat. Dhrishtadyumna wounds Kritavarma and covers him with arrows, but Kritavarma matches him. Dhrishtadyumna then kills Kritavarma's charioteer, and his Kaurava opponents surge forward for another round of fighting.
